- [ES2014a:18:29] The group discussed the function of the prototype and decided that they should restrict the remote to television for the time being instead of allowing it to control multiple devices.
- [ES2014b:29:34] The remote will feature a locator function that responds to clapping.
- [ES2014b:30:08] There will be a device that allows the user to enter two numbers separately to get a two-digit number in order to reduce the overall number of buttons.
- [ES2014b:33:40] The remote will feature a panel that hides complicated functions on the back of the device.
- [ES2014b:35:39] Buttons to adjust picture quality, channel tuning, and other settings will be hidden in this panel; the number pad, the channel- and volume-changing and power buttons will remain on the main interface.
- [ES2014c:34:34] The remote will feature push buttons instead of scroll buttons, and a kinetic power supply.
- [ES2014c:13:18] The remote will contain a simple chip.
- [ES2014c:18:14] The group decided to focus on a basic remote that will appeal to the widest market.
- [ES2014c:18:39] They also decided to market the speech recognition component as a "finder function" so as not to confuse it with more advanced speech recognition components in other remote controls.
- [ES2014c:25:32] The group decided to make the standby button in the shape of an apple.
- [ES2014c:27:31] The remote will also feature a rubber case and rubber buttons, and a single-curved design.
- [ES2014c:29:59] The remote will feature the company logo, possibly in a sticker form.
